Package de.labathome.trustconstr

Class QPSubproblem

java.lang.Object
de.labathome.trustconstr.QPSubproblem
public class QPSubproblem extends Object
Quadratic-programming subproblem helpers used inside the trust-region SQP / IP loops: the projected-CG inner solver, the equality-constrained KKT direct factorization, the modified-dogleg trust-region step, and the segment/box/sphere intersection routines that drive trust-region step acceptance.

    • eqpKktFact

      public static Matrix[] eqpKktFact(Matrix H, Matrix c, Matrix A, Matrix b)
      Solve the equality-constrained quadratic program 
         minimize  q(x) = 1/2 x^T G x + x^T c
   subject to    A x = b
      where G is the symmetric n x n Hessian, c, x are length-n vectors, and A is the m x n Jacobian of constraints (with m &le; n).

      See Nocedal & Wright, Numerical Optimization, 2nd ed. (2006), chapter 16.1.

      Parameters:
      H - n x n Hessian matrix of the EQP problem
      c - length-n gradient of the quadratic objective function
      A - m x n Jacobian matrix of the equality constraints
      b - length-m right-hand side of the constraint equation, sign-flipped
      Returns:
      two-element array [x, lambda] containing the solution and Lagrange multipliers

    • boxSphereIntersectionsWithExtraInfo

      public static IntersectionResult[] boxSphereIntersectionsWithExtraInfo(double[] z, double[] d, double[] lb, double[] ub, double trustRadius, boolean entireLine)
      Find the intersection between segment (or line) and box/sphere constraints.

      Find the intersection between the segment (or line) defined by the parametric equation x(t) = z + t*d, the rectangular box lb <= x <= ub and the ball ||x|| <= trust_radius.

      Parameters:
      z - [n] initial point
      d - [n] direction
      lb - [n] lower bounds to each one of the components of x, used to delimit the rectangular box
      ub - [n] upper bounds to each one of the components of x, used to delimit the rectangular box
      trustRadius - ball radius
      entireLine - When true, the function returns the intersection between the line x(t) = z + t*d (t can assume any value) and the constraints. When false, the function returns the intersection between the segment x(t) = z + t*d, 0 <= t <= 1 and the constraints.
      Returns:
      [3] The first element is the combined intersection result. The second element is the intersection result from sphereIntersections. The third element is the intersection result from boxIntersections.

    • modifiedDogleg

      public static Matrix modifiedDogleg(Matrix A, Object Y, Matrix b, double trustRadius, double[] lb, double[] ub)
      Approximately minimize 1/2 ||A x + b||^2 subject to ||x|| &lt; Delta and lb &le; x &le; ub using a modified dogleg approach. Implementation based on Byrd-Hribar-Nocedal (1999), pp.885-886.
      Parameters:
      A - m x n matrix in the minimization problem (m &lt; n expected)
      Y - Matrix or LinearOperator that applies the projection Q = A^T (A A^T)^-^1; for any input x, y = Q x is the minimum-norm solution of A y = x
      b - length-m vector in the minimization problem
      trustRadius - trust radius Delta (sphere boundary)
      lb - length-n lower bounds; Double.NEGATIVE_INFINITY disables the bound for that component. Algorithm assumes lb &le; 0
      ub - length-n upper bounds; Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY disables the bound for that component. Algorithm assumes ub &ge; 0
      Returns:
      length-n solution vector

    • projectedCG

      public static CGInfo projectedCG(LinearOperator H, Matrix c, Object Z, Object Y, Matrix b)
      Solve the equality-constrained quadratic program 
         minimize    1/2 x^T H x + x^T c
   subject to  A x + b = 0
      with the projected conjugate-gradient method. Convenience overload with no trust-region or box constraints.
      Parameters:
      H - operator that computes H v on a length-n vector
      c - length-n gradient of the quadratic objective
      Z - Matrix or LinearOperator that projects x into the null space of A
      Y - Matrix or LinearOperator that, given b, returns the minimum-norm solution of A x + b = 0
      b - length-m right-hand side of the constraint equation
      Returns:
      solution vector and additional CG info

    • projectedCG

      public static CGInfo projectedCG(LinearOperator H, Matrix c, Object Z, Object Y, Matrix b, double trustRadius, double[] lb, double[] ub, double tolerance)
      Solve EQP problem with projected CG method.

      Solve equality-constrained quadratic programming problem min 1/2 x^T H x + x^t c subject to A x + b = 0 and, possibly, to trust region constraints ||x|| < trust_radius and box constraints lb <= x <= ub.

      Without spherical or box constraints and with enough iterations, the method returns the exact optimum. With those constraints active, the returned value is only an inexpensive approximation.

      Parameters:
      H - operator that computes H v on a length-n vector
      c - length-n gradient of the quadratic objective
      Z - Matrix or LinearOperator that projects x into the null space of A
      Y - Matrix or LinearOperator that, given b, returns the minimum-norm solution of A x + b = 0
      b - length-m right-hand side of the constraint equation
      trustRadius - trust-region radius; Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY disables the trust-region constraint
      lb - length-n lower bounds; Double.NEGATIVE_INFINITY disables the bound for that component
      ub - length-n upper bounds; Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY disables the bound for that component
      tolerance - termination tolerance for the projected residual
      Returns:
      solution vector and additional CG info

    • projectedCG

      public static CGInfo projectedCG(LinearOperator H, Matrix c, Object Z, Object Y, Matrix b, double trustRadius, double[] lb, double[] ub, double tolerance, long maxIterations, long maxInfeasibleIterations, boolean returnAll)
      Solve the equality-constrained quadratic program 
         minimize    1/2 x^T H x + x^T c
   subject to  A x + b = 0
   and (optionally) ||x|| < trustRadius, lb ≤ x ≤ ub
      with the projected conjugate-gradient method (Algorithm 6.2 of Gould-Hribar-Nocedal, 2001).

      Without spherical or box constraints and with enough iterations, the method returns the exact optimum. With those constraints active, the returned value is only an inexpensive approximation.

      Parameters:
      H - operator that computes H v
      c - length-n gradient of the quadratic objective
      Z - Matrix or LinearOperator projecting into null(A)
      Y - Matrix or LinearOperator for the minimum-norm solution of A x + b = 0
      b - length-m right-hand side of the constraint equation
      trustRadius - trust-region radius; Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY disables the trust-region constraint
      lb - length-n lower bounds (use -inf to disable per dim)
      ub - length-n upper bounds (use +inf to disable per dim)
      tolerance - termination tolerance for the projected residual
      maxIterations - max CG iterations; -1 for the default n - m
      maxInfeasibleIterations - max iterations spent infeasible w.r.t. box constraints; -1 for the default n - m
      returnAll - if true, the result includes the iterate trajectory
      Returns:
      solution vector and additional CG info
